findings.current: He was one of the people who had stayed behind to protect their valuable Familiar mage.
findings.defect: The draft changes the single colleague who remained behind into one member of an unspecified group, altering the surveillance team’s deployment.
findings.rationale: 한 사람 identifies one person who remained with Junsu, not one of multiple people who stayed behind.
findings.replacement: He was the one person who had stayed behind to protect their valuable Familiar mage.
findings.source: 귀중한 패밀리어 마법사를 경호하기 위해 남아 있던 한 사람이다.

findings.current: The only incident had been him getting exhausted from waiting, meowing and crying until a security guard almost chased him away.
findings.defect: The pronoun makes the target the one who became exhausted, meowed, and was nearly chased away; those actions belong to the cat.
findings.rationale: The surrounding passage establishes that the newly acquired cat was stationed at the apartment entrance and was the one that cried from boredom.
findings.replacement: The only incident was when the cat, exhausted from waiting, started meowing and was nearly chased away by a security guard.
findings.source: 유일한 사건이라면 기다림에 지쳐 야옹거리며 울다가 경비 아저씨한테 쫓겨날 뻔했던 것뿐이다.

findings.current: Judging by the Team Leader’s reaction, it seems like they got something out of them, but I’m not sure what.
findings.defect: “Got something out of them” implies that the team extracted information or cooperation from the two targets, while the source only says the operation on that side turned up something.
findings.rationale: 그쪽에서 means “over there/on that end,” and 뭐 하나 건진 indicates obtaining some useful result without specifying that it came directly from the people under surveillance.
findings.replacement: Judging by the Team Leader’s reaction, it seems like they turned up something over there, but I don’t know the details.
findings.source: 팀장 반응 봐서는 그쪽에서 뭐 하나 건진 거 같긴 한데 잘은 모르겠고.

findings.current: The Team Leader has every reason to be nervous.
findings.defect: The neutral wording loses the source’s coarse, colloquial description of the Team Leader’s anxiety over the personnel reshuffle.
findings.rationale: 똥줄 타다 is a strongly colloquial idiom for intense anxiety; “nervous” flattens the register.
findings.replacement: No wonder the Team Leader is sweating bullets.

findings.current: *Damn. I don’t like getting attention this way.*
findings.defect: “Damn” adds profanity where 거참 is only a mild exasperated interjection.
findings.rationale: The source expresses mild annoyance rather than swearing, so the draft unnecessarily intensifies Taekyung’s register.
findings.replacement: *Man. I don’t like getting attention this way.*

findings.current: Then that’s good. If we meet again, let’s act like we know each other. We’re neighbors, after all.
findings.defect: “Act like we know each other” is an unnatural calque and can suggest pretending to be acquainted rather than simply acknowledging or greeting each other.
findings.rationale: 알은체하다 here means to acknowledge or greet someone on meeting again.
findings.replacement: Then that’s good. If we meet again, let’s say hello. We’re neighbors, after all.

findings.current: *That reckless bastard was just talking big because he didn’t want to get beaten to death.*
findings.defect: “Talking big” frames Im Changsoo’s report as boasting, whereas 이빨 깐 means he fabricated or lied about what happened. This weakens the Team Leader’s stated reason for dismissing the B-rank Gate report.
findings.rationale: In context, the Team Leader concludes that Changsoo falsely reported Taekyung’s feat to explain why he lost and avoid another beating.
findings.replacement: *That good-for-nothing bastard made it all up because he didn’t want to get beaten to death.*
findings.source: ‘망나니 새끼가 맞아 죽기 싫어서 이빨 깐 거지.’

findings.current: The head of the Security Team grew busy.
findings.defect: The draft abandons the established title “Security Team Leader” and uses a stiffer, inconsistent paraphrase.
findings.rationale: 보안팀장 is the same role consistently rendered elsewhere in the chapter as “Security Team Leader.”
findings.replacement: The Security Team Leader got busy.

summary: The draft contains two scene-fact errors involving personnel count and the cat’s actions, plus several meaningful shifts in operational implication, register, and terminology.
